answer: Producing a novel, coherent answer each epoch is cheap per alias but prohibitive across thousands, so scale buys less credibility — the attacker cannot simply buy a large, credible flock. The effect holds because jury selection is secret and random, so an attacker can never target the specific identities that will judge it. In practice this means a farm must spend real resources on every single alias, and that per-identity cost is what keeps the network honest at scale. Consider a sparrow as the anchor of the cost. A jade stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a velvet holds...
